name: Duda
tagline: Build and manage one client-ready responsive site from reusable sections

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day White Label trial with no credit card
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual plans billed upfront
pricing.hiddenCosts: The account plan only includes 1 site on Basic/Team or 4 on Agency/White Label; every extra published site is billed separately. AI Visibility starts at $19/month after its 14-day free period, and ecommerce/bookings plans are separate add-ons.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Duda, build and manage one client-ready responsive site from reusable sections. The hard boundary is agency workflow, white-labeling, hosting, client permissions, and support, plus editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem.
coreLoopDIY: Assemble one client-ready responsive site from reusable sections, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
whatYouLose: agency workflow, white-labeling, hosting, client permissions, and support
moatNotes: editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem
ongoingBurden: responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Duda because the page renderer is reproducible, but customers pay to avoid becoming their own hosting and browser-compatibility team. The recurring cost buys responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Webstudio
priorArt.desc: Open-source visual website builder designed around web standards.

alternatives.name: Concrete CMS
alternatives.desc: In-page editing, reusable blocks, permissions and workflows; hosting and client support are no longer bundled.

facts.install: Release ZIP to PHP hosting, create a MySQL/MariaDB database, then finish the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, settings and block data in SQL; uploaded assets in the server file manager or a configured remote storage location
facts.gapVsPaid: Concrete CMS lacks Duda's agency-first white-label dashboard, client billing/handoff workflow and managed hosting.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP hosting, a database, writable directories, and responsibility for updates, backups and outbound mail

alternatives.name: Plasmic
alternatives.desc: Reusable components, collaboration and unlimited projects free; client handoff is less agency-tailored.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optional npm-installed Plasmic CLI for React code generation and deployment in your own repository
facts.engines: Plasmic AI (beta); the official site does not name its underlying model provider
facts.dataFormat: Hosted projects and CMS records in Plasmic Cloud; codegen writes React components plus plasmic.json and plasmic.lock into the user's repository
facts.gapVsPaid: Plasmic lacks Duda's agency-specific white-label dashboard, client billing and standardized multi-site handoff workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Free hosted output keeps Plasmic branding; codegen/self-deployment requires a Node/React project and deployment workflow

alternatives.name: Silex
alternatives.desc: A free visual publisher for client sites with export; reusable-section workflows are basic.

facts.install: Use the hosted editor with a GitLab login, install the desktop alpha, or run the official Docker setup
facts.engines: Optional desktop MCP workflow can connect to Ollama, OpenCode, Goose or Claude Code
facts.dataFormat: Project JSON and assets in GitLab, FTP or local storage; publishing produces ordinary static HTML, CSS and JavaScript
facts.gapVsPaid: Silex's reusable sections, permissions, collaboration and client handoff are basic beside Duda's agency workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The stable hosted route starts with a GitLab account; the desktop build is still labelled alpha

alternatives.name: Vvveb
alternatives.desc: A visual CMS with multisite support, reusable themes and forms; the agency dashboard is less civilized.

facts.install: Download and upload the PHP release, open the site URL, and complete the browser installer
facts.dataFormat: Content, products, orders and settings in MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite or PostgreSQL; media and downloadable files on the server filesystem
facts.gapVsPaid: Vvveb has no comparably polished agency dashboard, white-label client workflow or managed fleet of sites.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP hosting, a database, writable files, mail and payment configuration, plus ongoing server updates

alternatives.name: Webstudio
alternatives.desc: Responsive visual sites with reusable components and CMS data; agency management becomes your own process.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; alternatively export the project or deploy the self-hosted builder/site
facts.engines: Webstudio Inception AI and MCP integrations; the hosted model provider is not named in official documentation
facts.dataFormat: Projects and assets live in Webstudio Cloud when hosted there; export/self-host routes produce source or static assets under the user's deployment
facts.gapVsPaid: Webstudio has no built-in agency billing, white-label client portal or managed multi-client workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The free cloud plan publishes only to a Webstudio subdomain; a free custom domain requires export or self-hosting

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: An embeddable editor developers use to build Duda-like products, not Duda-like product itself.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a single-site builder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Duda in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and static export; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: assemble one client-ready responsive site from reusable sections, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Provide a section library for hero, proof, features, pricing, FAQ, and footer blocks.
Use a constrained design-token system rather than arbitrary CSS controls.
Allow inline text editing and local image upload with responsive optimization.
Preview desktop, tablet, and mobile widths and surface overflow errors.
Persist projects in SQLite and support a portable JSON export.
Generate a clean static Next.js output and document deployment to one target.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace.
Deliberately leave out multi-tenant managed hosting.
Deliberately leave out advanced ecommerce, memberships, and agency billing.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
